questions.question: What is the core conceptual objective of a retrosynthetic disconnection in organic synthesis?

options.label: A
options.text: To predict the infrared spectrum of the target molecule.

options.label: B
options.text: To identify strategic C-C or C-heteroatom bonds whose hypothetical cleavage reveals simpler, commercially available precursor synthons.

options.label: C
options.text: To convert all chiral centers to achiral conformations.

options.label: D
options.text: To calculate the thermodynamic entropy of the overall reaction.

questions.correct_answer: To identify strategic C-C or C-heteroatom bonds whose hypothetical cleavage reveals simpler, commercially available precursor synthons.
questions.explanation: Retrosynthesis deconstructs complex targets step-by-step into simpler precursor materials using known forward reactions.

questions.question: In retrosynthetic analysis, what is the relationship between an acyl synthon [R-C⁺=O] and its synthetic equivalent?

options.label: A
options.text: The synthetic equivalent is always a radical.

options.label: B
options.text: The synthon is a real isolated molecule and the synthetic equivalent is imaginary.

options.label: C
options.text: They are resonance structures of each other.

options.label: D
options.text: The synthon is an idealized reactive fragment (R-C⁺=O), while the acyl chloride (R-COCl) is the actual laboratory reagent carrying out that reactivity.

questions.correct_answer: The synthon is an idealized reactive fragment (R-C⁺=O), while the acyl chloride (R-COCl) is the actual laboratory reagent carrying out that reactivity.
questions.explanation: Synthons are idealized ionic/radical fragments; synthetic equivalents are real, shelf-stable chemical reagents.

questions.question: What does a Functional Group Interconversion (FGI) accomplish in a forward synthetic sequence?

options.label: A
options.text: It racemizes all stereocenters.

options.label: B
options.text: It rearranges the carbon skeleton into an aromatic ring.

options.label: C
options.text: It transforms one functional group into another without altering the underlying carbon skeleton, preparing the molecule for a subsequent strategic step.

options.label: D
options.text: It cleaves the carbon chain into equal halves.

questions.correct_answer: It transforms one functional group into another without altering the underlying carbon skeleton, preparing the molecule for a subsequent strategic step.
questions.explanation: FGI modifies functional groups (e.g., alcohol to halide) to enable subsequent bond-forming or selective transformation steps.

questions.question: How does triethylsilyl chloride (TESCl) protect an alcohol against strong organometallic bases?

options.label: A
options.text: The alcohol oxygen attacks silicon in an SN2-Si displacement with chloride loss, converting the acidic O-H into a base-inert silyl ether (-OSiEt₃).

options.label: B
options.text: The silyl group protonates the organometallic reagent.

options.label: C
options.text: TESCl forms an ionic salt precipitate with the alcohol.

options.label: D
options.text: Silicon oxidizes the alcohol to a carboxylic acid.

questions.correct_answer: The alcohol oxygen attacks silicon in an SN2-Si displacement with chloride loss, converting the acidic O-H into a base-inert silyl ether (-OSiEt₃).
questions.explanation: Silyl ethers mask acidic hydroxyl protons, preventing unwanted acid-base quenching when using Grignard or organolithium reagents.

questions.question: Why does tetra-n-butylammonium fluoride (TBAF) selectively cleave silyl ether protecting groups?

options.label: A
options.text: Silicon has an exceptionally high thermodynamic affinity for fluoride (Si-F bond energy ~570 kJ/mol), driving rapid nucleophilic displacement at silicon.

options.label: B
options.text: Fluoride acts as a powerful reducing agent.

options.label: C
options.text: TBAF protonates the silicon atom.

options.label: D
options.text: Fluoride oxidizes the oxygen atom to peroxide.

questions.correct_answer: Silicon has an exceptionally high thermodynamic affinity for fluoride (Si-F bond energy ~570 kJ/mol), driving rapid nucleophilic displacement at silicon.
questions.explanation: The immense strength of the Si-F bond drives thermodynamic cleavage of silyl ethers under mild, neutral conditions.

questions.question: Why is a convergent synthetic strategy dramatically superior to a linear sequence for synthesizing large molecules?

options.label: A
options.text: Convergent synthesis eliminates all transition states.

options.label: B
options.text: Linear synthesis always produces racemic mixtures.

options.label: C
options.text: Convergent synthesis couples pre-assembled complex fragments in the final steps, minimizing the compounding penalty of fractional yields across long linear sequences.

options.label: D
options.text: Convergent synthesis does not require any purification.

questions.correct_answer: Convergent synthesis couples pre-assembled complex fragments in the final steps, minimizing the compounding penalty of fractional yields across long linear sequences.
questions.explanation: Linear yield compounds multiplicatively (0.8^10 ≈ 10.7%), whereas convergent coupling of two 5-step halves yields ~33% overall.

questions.question: How can a chemist selectively reduce a ketone in the presence of an ester within the same molecule?

options.label: A
options.text: By utilizing excess lithium aluminum hydride (LiAlH₄) at 100°C.

options.label: B
options.text: By irradiating with UV light.

options.label: C
options.text: By utilizing sodium borohydride (NaBH₄), which reduces electrophilic aldehydes and ketones rapidly but is inert toward less electrophilic esters.

options.label: D
options.text: By adding concentrated sulfuric acid.

questions.correct_answer: By utilizing sodium borohydride (NaBH₄), which reduces electrophilic aldehydes and ketones rapidly but is inert toward less electrophilic esters.
questions.explanation: NaBH₄ is a mild reducing agent that exhibits high chemoselectivity for ketones/aldehydes over esters and amides.

questions.question: What synthetic strategy ensures clean conversion of 2-bromopentane to 1-pentene rather than 2-pentene?

options.label: A
options.text: Using a sterically bulky base like potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) to enforce kinetic Hofmann elimination at the terminal methyl group.

options.label: B
options.text: Using sodium hydroxide in water at 100°C.

options.label: C
options.text: Using concentrated sulfuric acid.

options.label: D
options.text: Using sodium iodide in acetone.

questions.correct_answer: Using a sterically bulky base like potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) to enforce kinetic Hofmann elimination at the terminal methyl group.
questions.explanation: Bulky alkoxide bases selectively abstract accessible terminal protons, overriding thermodynamic Zaitsev selectivity.

questions.topic: Strategic C-C Bond Construction via Alkynylation
questions.question: What is the key advantage of using terminal alkynes as building blocks in carbon chain extension?

options.label: A
options.text: Alkynes only react via free radical mechanisms.

options.label: B
options.text: Alkynes cannot be oxidized or reduced.

options.label: C
options.text: Alkynes are inert toward all electrophiles.

options.label: D
options.text: The terminal sp C-H can be deprotonated to an acetylide carbanion, which acts as a powerful nucleophile in SN2 alkylations and carbonyl additions.

questions.correct_answer: The terminal sp C-H can be deprotonated to an acetylide carbanion, which acts as a powerful nucleophile in SN2 alkylations and carbonyl additions.
questions.explanation: Terminal alkynes provide a nucleophilic carbon center for C-C bond formation, with the resulting triple bond ready for diverse functionalizations.

questions.question: In designing a stereoselective synthesis of cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, which sequence is optimal?

options.label: A
options.text: Free radical bromination followed by sodium ethoxide.

options.label: B
options.text: Synthesis of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene followed by heterogeneous catalytic hydrogenation (H₂ / Pt), which guarantees syn addition across the π bond.

options.label: C
options.text: mCPBA epoxidation followed by aqueous acid hydrolysis.

options.label: D
options.text: Birch reduction using sodium in liquid ammonia.

questions.correct_answer: Synthesis of 1,2-dimethylcyclohexene followed by heterogeneous catalytic hydrogenation (H₂ / Pt), which guarantees syn addition across the π bond.
questions.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation over solid metal delivers both hydrogen atoms to the same face of the alkene, forging the cis stereoisomer.
